newsitem.title: USA: Board to hear AMR, pilot issues next week.
newsitem.headline: Board to hear AMR, pilot issues next week.

text.p: AMR Corp's American Airlines and its pilots will put their cases for a work contract before a presidential emergency board starting next week, the board's chairman said on Wednesday.
The hearing will begin on Thursday, Robert Harris said.
President Clinton named the board shortly after midnight last Friday, minutes after American's 9,300 pilots went on strike following a week of fruitless negotiations.
Under law, creation of a presidential emergency board forces strikers back to work for 60 days.
Harris said American and its pilots, members of the Allied Pilots Association, would present information to the three-member board for five days in Washington.
He said further information would be asked of American and the pilots as necessary.

The negotiations were stymied over pay and who should fly the new commuter jets American is planning to buy for its American Eagle regional carrier -- APA pilots, who make an average of $120,000 a year or Eagle's lower-paid pilots.
Harris said that after 30 days the board would write a description of the dispute as they saw it, in effect recommending a resolution.
Under the U.S. Railway Labor Act, which covers airline disputes, the two sides will then have 30 more days to consider the proposal and accept it or reject it.
If they reject it, the union is free to strike, although Congress could step in and require the two sides to enter binding arbitration.
